lastMessage:
Both confirmed:

1. The ScheduleWakeup error â€” harmless, my own tool misuse, self-corrected immediately. That tool is scoped to /loop dynamic-mode pacing, not general "wait for a background task" â€” I reached for it out of habit to wait on the clone-and-rebuild test, it correctly rejected the call (prompt is required unless stop:true, and I hadn't set either), and no wakeup, no loop state, no side effect resulted. I then did the actually-correct thing: nothing â€” the harness notifies me automatically when a backgrounded Bash task finishes, so polling or scheduling a wakeup for it would have been redundant even if the call had succeeded. Nothing to look into further.

2. The two failed Project-note edits â€” text-mismatch, not a stale-version conflict, and nothing was lost. Both failures were Edit's "String to replace not found in file" â€” I'd reconstructed the oldstring using plain hyphens (-) where the actual file uses em dashes (â€”), so the match failed. Edit fails atomically on a no-match: zero bytes get written when that happens, so there was never a partial or corrupted write to worry about â€” it's a pure no-op, not a merge conflict (nothing else was writing to that file concurrently). I fixed it by Read-ing the file to get the exact current bytes and anchoring on a shorter, more distinctive string, which matched on the third attempt.

I just re-read the section fresh to double check rather than trust my own memory of it: the robots.txt compliance paragraph appears exactly once, in the right place between "prompt-injection surface" and "Legal guardrail as an actual form field," and everything around it â€” the prompt-injection paragraph, the legal-guardrail paragraph, the meta.json additions list â€” is byte-identical to before. Nothing duplicated, nothing dropped.
